items.titulo: Discord's December 15 policy names ad IDs it collects on sponsored content
items.resumen: Impressions, clicks and conversions from ad partners enter Discord's privacy policy for anyone who engages with Quests. How much can new settings switch off?

items.titulo: Comic: Wishful Thinking
items.resumen: Enjoy this weekly comic strip from AdExchanger.com that highlights the digital advertising ecosystem … and happy Thanksgiving, everyone! The post Comic: Wishful Thinking appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: ChatGPT Ads New Call-To-Actions, Business Agents Beyond US, More Audience Metrics & More
items.resumen: OpenAI just sent out a product update on ChatGPT Ads announcing that Business Agents expand outside the U.S., new learn more call-to-action added to single image ads, more audience metrics in Ads Manager and the Ads API, ability to hide product feed sale prices when a promotion ends and new policy center details in Ads Manager.

items.titulo: OpenAI Isn’t Planning Prompt-Level Reports For ChatGPT Ads via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
items.resumen: OpenAI says ChatGPT advertisers can see aggregate results but won’t get reports showing the prompts or intent behind their ads. The post OpenAI Isn’t Planning Prompt-Level Reports For ChatGPT Ads appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.titulo: Google Adds Pageburst & 11 Other Existing Bots To Its Crawler Docs via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
items.resumen: Google's crawler docs now list pageburst, which renders pages for Google Ads and ignores robots.txt, plus more existing user agents to check in server logs. The post Google Adds Pageburst & 11 Other Existing Bots To Its Crawler Docs appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.titulo: Google Local Pack No Reviews Bug
items.resumen: Google is not showing reviews in the local pack for some business listings that do indeed have reviews. Google shows "No reviews" with no stars in the local pack for these businesses, but when you click on the listing, Google does show that these businesses have reviews.

items.titulo: Amazon lets advertisers change bids by where and when a video ad plays
items.resumen: Four placement types and four roll positions can now raise or lower bids, for online video ad groups only. Which buys are left out, and what stays undocumented?

items.titulo: Google patent describes an AI TV channel that stars the viewer
items.resumen: Viewing history, age, gender and a profile photo feed the AI prompt, and claim 4 covers stitching ads into each video. Whether a product follows is not stated.

items.titulo: YouTube's free phone editor now stacks video, text and sound in layers
items.resumen: Captions, overlay clips and several audio tracks each get a row that creators can mute or hide. YouTube has not said how many tracks fit, or in which markets.

items.titulo: Vermont bans feeds built on kids' data from January 1, 2027
items.resumen: Age checks must erase a child's data at once, keeping only an age range, under two Vermont rules for apps used by minors. What changed after the July draft?

items.titulo: Fast fashion, slow parcels: SHEIN to pay the FTC $100m
items.resumen: Five phone agents for nearly 1m US parcels a day, the FTC alleges. The order sets delay notices and review rules for SHEIN. When will buyers see their refunds?

items.titulo: Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads drops to $4.99 a month for a year
items.resumen: Premium falls to $14.99 from $21.99 for new and returning US sign-ups through November 30. What do cheaper sign-ups to the ad plan mean for Disney ad sales?

items.titulo: X wins UK judgment against two users it says took £207,384 in creator pay
items.resumen: Six linked accounts drew the money from 2023 to 2026, X alleges. Neither defendant answered, so damages and costs now wait for a hearing with no date set yet.

items.titulo: Best-of lists climb to 65% of AI Black Friday toy links, iPullRank finds
items.resumen: Brand websites got no lift in AI answers as Black Friday 2025 neared, and ChatGPT runs about two weeks ahead this year. Data for 2026 lands after Cyber Monday.

items.titulo: Device and app makers face German fines up to 2.5% of sales from 2027
items.resumen: Germany's cyber agency starts approving product test labs tomorrow and plans 141 posts by 2029. What can it enforce before fines arrive on December 11, 2027?

items.titulo: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy exits after more than 11 years
items.resumen: Product and technology chief Balaji Thiagarajan and the board now run a marketplace of 1.4 million sellers. A successor is due in weeks; no listing date is set.

items.titulo: Wall Street Journal tells all bots to keep out, except more than 60
items.resumen: Search crawlers and three OpenAI scrapers made the guest list, and Barron's and MarketWatch share the rule. Can a file bots may ignore get AI firms to pay?

items.titulo: OpenAI adds over 2,000 internet addresses ChatGPT uses to visit websites
items.resumen: Sites that verify ChatGPT visits by address now meet 130 new blocks, taking the list from 237 to 367 entries. What the capacity is for, OpenAI has not said.

items.titulo: ESPN's first Super Bowl will play live in IMAX theaters
items.resumen: Hundreds of IMAX screens in the US and abroad, Australia and Brazil included, carry the game on February 14, 2027. Will the commercial breaks reach theaters?

items.titulo: Prime Video renews Rings of Power for season 4 with no date or cast
items.resumen: Filming starts this spring at the UK's Shepperton Studios, no year given. Season 3 took about 17 months from cameras to screen. Will Prime members wait as long?

items.titulo: Amazon's CTO says the 20-watt brain will shape the next computers
items.resumen: IT chiefs now ask Werner Vogels about geopolitics before cost, and his 2027 list has company AI agents attacking code before launch. What changes for ad data?

items.titulo: Character.ai still faces Kentucky's chatbot lawsuit during bankruptcy
items.resumen: Louisville firm FBT Gibbons, owed $11,180.90, is named as local counsel in Kentucky's case. Objections close December 15, a week after the sale hearing ends.

items.titulo: Character.ai moves to keep the law firm it owes $146,382 on three lawsuits
items.resumen: Munger, Tolles & Olson lists past or current work for Google, OpenAI and Disney. Objections to its role in the three chatbot lawsuits are due by December 15.

items.titulo: KPMG could earn up to $5.1m finding Character.ai a California tax refund
items.resumen: Fees fall from 30% of the first $2m to 10% above $18m, paid only once California pays. The filing's own timeline runs to 10.5 years if the state pushes back.

items.titulo: Game: Quiet January dashboards flatter whoever kept spending
items.resumen: Sixteen terms in four groups to end the week. One set comes from this week's coverage, and the grown-up vocabulary refuses to stay in one place.

items.titulo: Daily Search Forum Recap: November 25, 2026
items.resumen: Here is a recap of what happened in the search forums today...

items.titulo: The typical Google Ads sale costs European shops 14% more, Channable finds
items.resumen: Median cost per sale went from €14.41 to €16.47 for over 10,000 EU online shops while click prices held flat. Will Black Friday weekend push the rise past 20%?

items.titulo: Google frees US candidates' business ads from election ad rules
items.resumen: Ads showing US officeholders as insurance or real estate agents skip election checks if politics stays out. Which ten regions still restrict political ads?

items.titulo: ChatGPT ad reports add 9 metrics built on how many people see the ads
items.resumen: OpenAI defines frequency as impressions divided by reach for ChatGPT advertisers. Business Agents leave the US too, but which countries qualify is unnamed.

items.titulo: ChatGPT ads start counting people as SHEIN pays $100m and fake TVs cost $135m
items.resumen: OpenAI added reach metrics to ChatGPT ads, the FTC settled with SHEIN for $100m, Pixalate priced a fake TV fraud at $135m and Amazon Autos headed to the UK.

items.titulo: In B2B, the safe brand beats the better product, LinkedIn argues
items.resumen: Being able to defend the choice topped five buyer motives at 34% among 750 senior B2B buyers. What about the finance and procurement staff that ads never reach?

items.titulo: YouTube quietly tests a mute button in its Android app
items.resumen: Spotted on Android app version 21.46.522, the speaker icon sits beside full screen for some users only. Would an ad silenced with it still count as a view?

items.titulo: Off-topic videos can draw 10 views or 10 million, YouTube tells creators
items.resumen: No channel-wide score exists in YouTube's algorithm, so a creator's million-view average promises nothing off-topic. Can a variety channel still hold together?

items.titulo: Trade Desk says direct connection lifted DAZN Media+ auction revenue 41%"
items.resumen: Bids sent direct to Kayo Sports, BINGE and Foxtel won 2.9 times as often as bids routed via middlemen. How much of the gain was new money is not disclosed.

items.titulo: Pixalate estimates fake TVs cost advertisers $135 million in six months
items.resumen: Fake TV identities that reset every midnight posed as 3,277 streaming apps, from Hulu to Tubi. Why did 77% arrive through sellers the apps never authorised?

items.titulo: LG lets DoubleVerify check its TV home screen ads for fraud
items.resumen: Menu tiles and other native formats are covered worldwide for brands already using DV. Does it reach the 26 markets where Teads holds LG home screen sales?

items.titulo: MonetizeMore says 10.8% of the traffic it checked was bots posing as people
items.resumen: Easy-to-catch bots were 0.4%. For ad buyers and publishers, its CEO says AWS's new auction filters see only the request. What can a check before the bid miss?

items.titulo: MNTN advertisers' site traffic rose in 15 of 26 industries after Christmas
items.resumen: Fitness studios led at 74%, hotels hit 37% and law offices 22% in median traffic gains for streaming TV advertisers. One platform's data, ahead of January 2027.

items.titulo: No sale, no pay: Taboola links 60 brands with 21,000 creators
items.resumen: Howl, the creator network Taboola bought in August, claims over $1.5bn in gross sales. Brands pay only per sale, so sales tracking sets what each brand pays.

items.titulo: Amazon counts a shopper's rating as the click advertisers pay for
items.resumen: No fee for impressions or for shoppers who skip the card, for US brands with products under 1,000 reviews. Rating counts in API reports still await an update.

items.titulo: Amazon adds five metrics to count sales from Netflix ads
items.resumen: Netflix ad buyers on Amazon now see purchases, sales, page visits and off-Amazon actions tied to Netflix views. Still unpublished: the rules behind each count.

items.titulo: Amazon ad reports now show what advertisers pay Barometer to vet podcasts
items.resumen: Two new Amazon report fields record Barometer's prebid fees for podcast buyers, six weeks after its DVA+ debut. One agency fee method also marks up that charge.

items.titulo: North America no longer has Amazon Ad Tag setup to itself
items.resumen: Accounts in Europe and the Far East can now create one Amazon Ad Tag each in Ads data manager, dataset included. What happens to tags built in Events Manager?

items.titulo: Amazon adjusts bids to chase the spending ad buyers promised publishers
items.resumen: Agency and brand commitments to publishers run 7 to 366 days and count media cost only, not buy-side fees. What happens to one when the publisher deletes it?

items.titulo: Amazon bans ads whose audio starts or stops abruptly, on every ad product
items.resumen: Ads with sound on Amazon need a mute button and can't outplay the content around them. Older guidance only advised against abrupt music cuts. Who must comply?

items.titulo: Amazon forces 7 kinds of gambling advertiser to prove licences before ads run
items.resumen: Some dating services face the same check, and fixed-odds betting ads in Brazil were banned in October. Amazon no longer says reviews slow down at busy times.

items.titulo: New Amazon ad accounts get two invoices, one just for sponsored ads
items.resumen: Invoice billing covers sponsored ads, Full-Funnel Campaigns and DVA+ alike for sellers, vendors and authors. Where balance deductions now fit is left unsaid.

items.titulo: AI agents linked to Amazon Ads get an optional upgrade on December 8
items.resumen: Agent builders on Amazon Ads need no action, and older protocol versions keep working with no end date. What changes for developers who opt into the new model?

items.titulo: Amazon's reporting guide catches up with its January 31, 2027 shutdown
items.resumen: Sponsored ads and DVA+ report pages close a month later than the December 31, 2026 date set in June. Which Amazon page still carries the old deadline today?

items.titulo: Amazon Autos to list Hyundai cars in the UK from early 2027
items.resumen: Vertu Motors is the first UK dealer group named, and shoppers reserve online but sign at the showroom. What Amazon charges dealers remains the open question.

items.titulo: Etsy plans to enforce its unedited-photo rule from early 2027
items.resumen: Cropping, resizing and watermarks are now allowed on the required photo if no AI tool touches it. Refunds apply already; which listings are exempt from it?

items.titulo: Amazon blocks 20 of 24 AI agents by name, the most of 79 top US retailers
items.resumen: Invitations to named AI agents at 79 big US chains rose from 1 in 2024 to 63 in 2026, with Ulta Beauty at 11. Does a written welcome actually let the bots in?
